title: Set Logger
text:
A simple container that collects the key-value pairs of the mrdHeader, metadata and ice header of each item, and reports the count of each value for each key appended to the end of the logs. This container makes no changes or alterations to the image data, metadata or header.
Container currently works with image-to-image and in available in Neurocontainers as such.
The SetLog module does have work in progress acquisition logging for raw-to-complex-image however this is still a WIP, to use it in a container the container must first be configured to a raw-2-complex image container.

Source code is available on my Github

title: MCPC-3D-S combination
text:
Overview
An image-to-image container that performs the MCPC-3D-S algorithm [1] with n-echo times and m-channels. Designed for immediate combination of images for later QSM analysis.

Source code is available on my Github
WARNING: This container suffers from long processing times, sequences with large total slice counts >50,000 have processing times over 30min. This is primarily a limitation on the scanner throughout of images and not strictly the container.


Parameters

Config (choice):

MCPC-3D-S Standard: The MCPC-3D-S Algorithm via Julia, source code can be found at [2]
MCPC-3D-S Memory Efficent: Recommended for larger scans
MCPC Logger: A dedicated logging for debugging

2pi Phase Scale (bool): scales images to [-2pi,2pi] if False images are scaled to [-pi,pi]
replaceGRAPPA (bool): Replaces GRAPPA Images with MCPC-3D-S Images, leave false to recieved both GRAPPA and MCPC-3D-S images.
Performance Timer (bool): Times each major step by the container.
SendOriginal (bool): Output uncombined images.



References
[1] Eckstein, K., Dymerska, B., Bachrata, B., Bogner, W., Poljanc, K., Trattnig, S., & Robinson, S. D. (2018). Computationally Efficient Combination of Multi-channel Phase Data From Multi-echo Acquisitions (ASPIRE). Magnetic resonance in medicine, 79(6), 2996–3006. https://doi.org/10.1002/mrm.26963
[2] https://github.com/korbinian90/ASPIRE (do properly)

title: CBS B0map Stats
text:
Overview
An image-to-image container that inputs a magnitude and two phase images and creates a B0map.
The container is available on the Neurocontainers Builder Site, or on the Neurodesk OpenRecon repository Github.
Source code is available on my Github


Config Parameters

Config (choice): There is no choice here the only option is the B0map script
Number of Dilations (int): the number of dilations performed on the Brain Mask. Dilations are performed using scipy.ndimage.binary_dilation() NOTE: Dilations happen before Erosions

Min: 0
Max: 100
Default: 2

Number of Erosions (int): the number of erosions performed on the Brain Mask. Erosions are performed using scipy.ndimage.binary_erosion() NOTE: Dilations happen before Erosions

Min: 0
Max: 100
Default: 3

Fractional Intensity (double): The fractional threshold of the BET2 brain mask, smaller values give larger brain outline estimates

Min: 0.0
Max: 1.0
Default: 0.4

Send Originals (boolean): When Send Originals is True the 2 magnitude and phase difference images are sent back unmodified.

Default: True

Gaussian Smoothing (boolean): Performs a gaussian smoothing of the B0map with a std==1. Smoothing is performed using scipy.ndimage.gaussian_filter()
TE1/TE2 (str): These two are optional and serve as a manual backup in case the echo times of the Mag 1 and Mag 2 images cannot be found. TE1 and TE2 are in units of milliseconds and they must be entered in as “3.06” not “3,06”. It is recommended to input these values if they are easily accessible in the Program Card.

TE1 Default: “10.00”
TE2 Default: “12.00”
Delta TE Default: “2.00”


NOTE: These are entered as string variables if they do not follow a float convention they will be disregarded.

Verbose Logging (boolean): Enables extra logging of data arrays and the B0map process steps.

Default: False

title: 🚀 ORLaunch
text:
WIP







Overview
Orlaunch is designed to streamline the process of creating new OpenRecon containers and the development process. Fundamentally its a customisable project-generator that populates a project directory based on a JSON template layout and template files. Additionally ORlaunch has some scripts to help with compiling your application in a container.
By default ORlaunch contains boilerplate code for python-based development however you can freely customise which boilerplate you use, via the template_map.json file (more info below).
Orlaunch is available on github


Features

Customisable project-folder scaffold via JSON files
Boilerplate code to kick-start container development.



How to use ORlaunch

Creating a new project
To create a new project, run:
python orlaunch new --project-name myproject --project-dir .
This creates a new project folder named myproject in your current directory and populates it with the following structure:
APP_NAME/
|
|-- App Code/
|   |-- APP_NAME.py
|   |-- ORUtils/
|   |   |-- Logger.py
|   |   |-- ...
|-- Utilities/
|   |-- Checks/
|   |   |-- CheckDockerVerison.py
|   |   |-- OpenReconSchema_1.1.0.json
|-- Dockerfile
|-- APP_NAME_Label.json
|-- APP_NAME_Documentation.md
|-- CreateContainer.py
|-- Containers/
